title: One of Lorca's Best Lines...
text:
one of Lorca's best lines

is,

"agony, always

agony..."

think of this when

you kill a

cockroach or

pick up a blade to

shave

waking in the morning

to

face the

sun
editorial_note: The translation keeps Bukowski's lowercase plainness and the Lorca line as a blunt morning refrain.

title: When You Are Young...
text:
when you are young

a pair

of women's

high-heeled

shoes

motionless

solitary

in the closet

can ignite

your bones;

when you are old

they are only

a pair of shoes

with

nobody

in them

and

nothing more.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the contrast between erotic charge in youth and emptied object in age.

title: The Best of the Breed
text:
there is nothing to

discuss

there is nothing to

remember

there is nothing to

forget

it is sad

and

it is not

sad

it seems that the

most

sensible

thing a person can

do

is

sit

with a glass in

hand
editorial_note: The translation keeps the stripped-down movement from negation to sitting with a drink.

title: I Met a Genius
text:
today

I met a genius on the train

about six years old;

he sat beside me and,

as the train

ran along the coast,

we came to the ocean.

the boy looked at me and said:

"the sea isn't pretty at all."


it was the first time

I realized

that.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the child's deflating statement and the speaker's sudden agreement.

title: Trapped
text:
do not undress my love

you might find a mannequin:

do not undress the mannequin

you might find

my love.


long ago she

forgot me.


she is trying on a new

hat

and looks more

coquettish

than ever.


she is a child

and a mannequin

and death.


I cannot hate

that


she did

nothing

out of the ordinary.


I only wanted

her to.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the mannequin/love/death substitutions and the bitter final expectation.
